output.review_comment: The validation, returning every team (including those with 0 desks), and exact `Fraction` quotients are correct and match the docstring. The blocker is the new `-allocation[team]` ("fewest desks already allocated") tie-breaker. The PR itself says it was added only so that `test_quarterly_floor_plan` passes. It contradicts the docstring, which says a tied quotient goes to the larger headcount, then to the team listed first. Tracing platform 60 / design 30 / support 16 with 6 desks under the documented rule: desk 2 is a tie at 30 that platform wins on headcount, and desk 6 is a tie at 15 that platform also wins. That gives 4/1/1, not the 3/2/1 the test expects. The new rule changes the result of every tie between teams with different desk counts, so it quietly redefines the method for all callers. The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth. Please remove the extra tie-breaker, implement the documented ordering (quotient, then headcount, then listed order), and tell the teammate that `test_quarterly_floor_plan`'s expected value conflicts with the docstring so they can decide whether the test or the spec should change. Minor: `order.index(team)` inside the key is O(n) per call. Precompute a position dict, or rely on `max` returning the first maximal item.
